title: Gauge Unification & Supersymmetry Archaeology
status: canonical science archaeology + externally audited gauge-unification research programme
abstract: This branch records Tim Dooley's recovered interest in M-theory, supersymmetry and higher-dimensional unification while separating those project prompts from later archive-added SU(4), SU(5), Spin(10) and supersymmetry machinery. The scientifically serious question is not whether several large symmetry groups can be named in one diagram, but whether one explicitly chosen gauge group, representation content and symmetry-breaking chain reproduces the Standard Model, yields consistent anomaly-free matter, predicts the running of couplings and produces observable consequences such as proton decay, neutrino structure, new gauge bosons or superpartner spectra. A genuine supersymmetric completion additionally requires a supersymmetry-breaking sector and a resulting mass spectrum; the super-Poincare algebra alone is not a phenomenological model. The archive therefore treats Pati-Salam, SU(5) and Spin(10) as alternative or nested model routes rather than cumulative evidence for Potatoverse theology. The current state is T1-T2: the representation-theory and renormalization-group toolkit is concrete, but no unique Timic GUT, breaking scale, threshold spectrum or distinctive prediction has been selected.
research_question: Can one explicitly chosen gauge/supersymmetry completion connect the recovered higher-dimensional unification programme to the Standard Model through a fully specified representation and symmetry-breaking chain, and does it make a quantitative prediction that survives current bounds?
maturity: T1-T2 archaeology/model-selection stage; no unique GUT/SUSY completion selected

standard_model_baseline.gauge_group: [SU(3)_C x SU(2)_L x U(1)_Y]/Gamma, with global quotient convention stated when relevant
standard_model_baseline.requirement: Any proposed unified representation must decompose to the observed low-energy chiral content and produce an acceptable Higgs/Yukawa sector.

pati_salam.scientific_value: Makes quark/lepton and left/right organization explicit and naturally introduces a right-handed neutrino degree of freedom in standard constructions.

su5.generation: bar5+10; optional singlet 1 for a right-handed neutrino
su5.key_observable: Heavy X/Y gauge bosons generically mediate baryon-number-violating processes such as proton decay in simple GUT realizations.

spin10.scientific_value: One chiral representation can organize a complete Standard Model generation plus nu_R, making representation compression genuinely stronger than a visual group analogy.

renormalization_group_contract.one_loop: mu dg_i/dmu=b_i g_i^3/(16 pi^2); equivalently d alpha_i^(-1)/d ln mu=-b_i/(2 pi)
renormalization_group_contract.normalization: For conventional SU(5)-normalized hypercharge use g_1=sqrt(5/3) g_Y, hence alpha_1=(5/3)alpha_Y. State the convention before plotting or comparing unification.
renormalization_group_contract.thresholds: Piecewise beta coefficients change when particles/fields enter or leave the effective spectrum. A credible unification plot must state the assumed masses and matching conditions.
renormalization_group_contract.test: Run measured low-energy couplings upward with the declared particle content and uncertainties; quantify whether they meet within threshold/model uncertainties rather than asserting visual convergence.
renormalization_group_contract.two_loop_rule: If numerical precision is used to argue for or against a serious model, include higher-loop running and threshold corrections appropriate to that claim.

supersymmetry_contract.meaning: This defines a graded spacetime symmetry structure; it does not determine a realistic low-energy spectrum.
model_requirements: soft terms or equivalent breaking data
supersymmetry_contract.natural_scale_warning: Writing the SUSY algebra does not imply superpartners must lie at any particular accessible mass; phenomenology depends on the breaking sector and spectrum.
observable_interfaces: dark-matter observables if a stable candidate is specified

symmetry_breaking_contract.rule: A group-subgroup arrow is a research plan until the field/vev that realizes the breaking is specified.

representation_and_anomaly_contract.representation_check: List every chiral fermion representation under the full gauge group and show how it decomposes at each breaking step.
representation_and_anomaly_contract.anomaly_check: Verify gauge and mixed anomalies cancel for the actual chiral spectrum; embedding in an anomaly-free unified representation may help but should be shown for the chosen model.
representation_and_anomaly_contract.charge_convention: Track right-handed fields versus all-left-chiral conjugate notation; apparent sign discrepancies in hypercharge/T3R often come from convention changes.

observable_program.proton_decay: A concrete GUT must calculate dominant operators/channels, mediator masses/couplings and lifetimes; experimental non-observation constrains the model's scale/structure.
observable_program.neutrinos: If nu_R/seesaw structure is part of the unification motivation, derive the mass matrix and connect it to neutrino masses/mixings rather than treating nu_R as only a representation-counting success.
observable_program.new_gauge_bosons: Intermediate or unified gauge bosons imply masses/couplings and therefore collider/precision/astrophysical constraints depending on the model.
observable_program.coupling_unification: Quantify a goodness-of-unification/matching residual under stated thresholds rather than presenting converging lines as proof.
observable_program.susy_spectrum: If SUSY is retained, compute at least a benchmark spectrum and the observables most sensitive to it.

model_selection_rule: Do not combine Pati-Salam, SU(5), Spin(10), E6, SUSY and 11D geometry into one claimed model unless the embeddings, field content and breaking chain are explicitly specified. Prefer one minimal route at a time and compare its explanatory compression and predictions.

falsification_and_failure_conditions: A proposed representation/breaking chain cannot reproduce the observed Standard Model chiral spectrum and charges.
Gauge/mixed anomalies remain uncancelled in the actual proposed spectrum.
Predicted proton-decay or new-particle rates conflict with experimental limits for the claimed parameter region.
Gauge couplings fail to meet within the declared threshold/higher-loop uncertainties when coupling unification is a stated prediction.
A supersymmetric model has no viable breaking/vacuum/spectrum consistent with the observables it invokes.
The model adds groups/fields without a quantitative prediction or explanatory compression beyond a simpler completion.
